newsitem.title: USA: Oil, gas producers cut reserve replacement costs.
newsitem.headline: Oil, gas producers cut reserve replacement costs.

text.p: Oil and natural gas producers continued to shave reserve replacement costs last year as new technologies cut exploration and development expenses, according to an analysis released on Wednesday by accounting firm Arthur Andersen.

Reserve replacement costs from all sources -- revisions, purchases and the drill bit -- fell 6 percent to $4.22 per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) on U.S. production, while replacement costs for production outside the United States fell modestly to $4.79 boe, the firm said in its annual report on oil and gas reserves of publicly held companies.

In addition to replacing reserves more efficiently, producers last year boosted capital spending to the highest level since 1992, fueled in large part by increased domestic spending by the major oil companies, said Victor Burk, managing director of the firm's energy practice in Houston.
"(The industry) is in its healthiest shape in over 15 years and has begun a period of strong domestic and international growth," Burk said.
Worldwide, producers in the study increased exploration and development spending to $50.4 billion, including $17.3 billion earmarked for drilling in the United States.

"In contrast with recent years, the majors are driving the increases in domestic as well as foreign spending. The entire increase in U.S. exploration and development expenditures -- $1.3 billion -- came from the majors," Burk said.

Royal Dutch/Shell Group spent $1.5 billion domestically as it stepped up deepwater projects in the Gulf of Mexico, while Amoco Corp spent $1.1 billion and Texaco Inc spent about $1 billion, the firm said.
Arthur Andersen's data on capital spending, reserve replacement costs and production replacement rates was culled from disclosures of 231 publicly owned oil and gas companies.
